solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Buy extra naughty see- through accessory?

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of the two words before it are made to misbehave and rearrange

explanation.surface: An invitation to buy something a bit risqué, perhaps see-through lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'see-through accessory' suggests racy clothing; the question mark warns it is really radiography kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatus producing radiographs lets doctors see through the body, so it is a whimsical 'see-through' device.

clue.text: Cook biting one expensive big cheese

indicators.note: biting means holding something between the teeth, so the cook's word wraps round the numeral's letter

parts.note: a cook in a restaurant is a chef
one is the Roman numeral I
executive as an adjective describes upmarket, costly goods, as in executive homes

explanation.surface: A cook takes a bite out of something pricey made of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important person, the boss of an organisation.

clue.text: Having run out of grains, pick dessert

indicators.note: out of says one thing is taken away from another, here the run's letter leaves the grains

parts.note: rice is a cereal eaten as grains
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the pick of something is its best part, the cream

explanation.surface: Someone who has no grain left chooses a pudding instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet treat served after a meal is a classic pudding, a dessert.

clue.text: Times article on top 60% of 6 in idyllic place

parts.note: the multiplication sign, times, is X
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue the top 60% of a five-letter word is its first three letters, the upper part of the entry

parts.note: 6 points to the answer at 6 down, meaning grown-up

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about the top portion of something, set in a perfect spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the five letters of the 6-down answer, 60% is three, so keep ADU.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's poem made Kubla Khan's summer palace a byword for a magnificent paradise.

clue.text: Arabic wife stopping money for cleaner of estate?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these letters fill the middle of the money word

parts.note: ready money is cash
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An Arab wife holding up the funds for someone who cleans a landed estate.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British station wagon, an estate car, not land.
explanation.definitionFit: The automatic facility at a garage cleans vehicles, including an estate car.

clue.text: Pupils encounter idea of marks in report?

parts.note: a group of pupils taught together is a class
an encounter can be a fight or struggle

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren grapple with how marks are presented on a school report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' said in a report sounds like Marx, whose theory of history is the conflict of social strata.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx's central idea was the conflict between social strata; 'marks' sounds like his name when reported.

clue.text: Developed area in the last month, freehold finally being accepted

indicators.note: being accepted means taken in, so the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of freehold

explanation.surface: Land was developed last month, with freehold finally granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully developed means grown-up or mature, as a fully grown animal is.

clue.text: Aggressive fool pursuing thrill

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the fool comes after the thrill

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, as in doing it for kicks
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A combative idiot chasing excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang adjective describes someone forceful and combative, so aggressive is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Look back, concerned with American president dividing opinion to cause uncertainty

indicators.note: back means the look word is read backwards

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
in can mean concerning, as in 'in business'

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the opinion word, so these letters sit within it

parts.note: sense can mean an opinion, as in the sense of the meeting

explanation.surface: Looking back at a divisive American president leaves people unsure.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone anxiously waiting for an outcome is to cause uncertainty in them.

clue.text: Persevering to lower current when holding right tool

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the right letter is held within the rest
in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the word

parts.note: soldiering on means persevering despite difficulty
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone persists in reducing the electric current while keeping a hand on the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lower' works because this is a down entry: the current's letter literally drops further down the word before the right letter is slotted in.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated hand implement used to melt metal alloy onto electrical joints is a tool.

clue.text: When solvers start to waver before getting back to normal

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a setter addresses solvers as you

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of waver

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Solvers begin to falter before recovering their normal state.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command tells troops to return to their previous position, so it means revert to normal.

clue.text: Fawn that's new in Sri Lanka

indicators.note: in places the new word inside the country's code

parts.note: CL is the international vehicle code for Sri Lanka
raw means new or inexperienced, as in a raw recruit

explanation.surface: A young deer that is new to Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like a young deer but is the verb: to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter obsequiously, which is to grovel or toady.

clue.text: Close society elite working to carry women to and fro

parts.note: to close is to shut

indicators.note: to carry means to hold inside, so the shuffled letters hold the women's letter
working means in operation, here reworking the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclusive society's elite are busy ferrying women back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges S plus ELITE into TLEISE, which then carries W.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving like a loom's bobbin means going backwards and forwards, to and fro.

clue.text: Instrument of torture finally taken on by monarchy

indicators.note: taken on by means added at the end, so the torture letter follows the monarchy

parts.note: the United Kingdom is a monarchy, UK for short

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of torture

explanation.surface: A torture device finally adopted by the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The small four-stringed ukulele is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Quits appearing in terribly amateurish film

indicators.note: appearing in means placed within, so the quits word sits inside the shuffled letters
terribly means badly, so the letters of amateurish are badly arranged

parts.note: being quits means being square, or evens

explanation.surface: Someone calls it quits after appearing in a dreadfully amateur movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' and 'evens' both describe a bet or debt that ends square; the anagram splits as a three-letter word before the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Akira Kurosawa's 1954 epic about hired warriors defending a village is a celebrated film.

clue.text: Former knight with no time for model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: a Knight Templar belonged to a medieval military order

explanation.surface: A former knight with no time left became a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example worth imitating is a model, as in a model pupil.

clue.text: Vixen perhaps using control that's excessive you say?

parts.note: to rein in is to control, and a rein is a means of control

indicators.note: you say signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: dear means expensive, excessive in price

explanation.surface: A female fox controlled by something excessive, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vixen' looks like a female fox, but is one of Santa's team.
explanation.definitionFit: Vixen is one of Santa Claus's team pulling his sleigh, so is an example of the animal.

clue.text: Awful element of British Guiana in revolt

indicators.note: in revolt means turned over, so the hidden letters are read backwards
element of means a part taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dreadful part of the colony of British Guiana rising up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element of' finds HGU spanning British Guiana; 'in revolt' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of disgust is what one says when something is awful.

clue.text: Leg and loin in hot pot without lid

parts.note: H is short for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: without lid means the top letter, in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: a pot is a pot belly, or paunch

explanation.surface: Cuts of leg and loin cooking in a hot pot with no lid.
explanation.definitionFit: The cut of meat comprising the leg and loin of a deer or sheep is the joint so named.

clue.text: Low-grade, gooey slimy fungi making colloid

parts.note: E is a low grade, as in exam marks

indicators.note: gooey means soft and sticky, so the letters lose shape and rearrange

explanation.surface: Poor-quality, sticky slimy mushrooms forming a gel-like substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersing oil into water forms a stable suspension, a kind of colloid.

clue.text: Scrap metal's ending in forge

indicators.note: in places the ending letter inside the forge word

parts.note: to forge is to fake

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of metal

explanation.surface: A piece of metal comes off in the blacksmith's forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forge' suggests a smithy, but it means counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin fragment or shaving is a scrap of material.

clue.text: Beef — good cut of beef

parts.note: rump is a cut of beef from the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A list of beef: good, then a cut of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' here is the verb or noun for a complaint or bad mood, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is to complain, and a bad-tempered complaint or sulk is a grouse.

clue.text: Foreigner, one taking heavy blow outside church

indicators.note: outside means the first pieces surround the church letters

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a lander is a heavy punch that lands
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An outsider takes a heavy punch outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a North Atlantic island nation is a foreigner to anyone elsewhere.

clue.text: Subject having son ousted by cold, isolated group

indicators.note: ousted by means replaced by, so the cold letter takes the son's place

parts.note: to subject someone is to enslave them
C is short for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A subject whose son has been driven out by a frosty, cut-off group.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket of people distinct from those around them is a cut-off community or group.

clue.text: Recognised that boy taking book inside — still here?

indicators.note: inside places the pieces within the recognised word

parts.note: seen means noticed or recognised
that boy is he

explanation.surface: Someone noticed that the boy took a book indoors; is he still there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is not 'yet' but a distilling apparatus; 'taking' just joins HE and B.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit Irish drinking den might house a still making moonshine.
